title: Ray McKinley and the Miller band
summary: McKinley drummed on one Sauter-Finegan session and led the Miller band.

bands.name: Glenn Miller Army Air Force Band

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: Sauter-Finegan record with us; did you know that?
Which one did he do? It could have been "Moonlight On The Ganges". It was one of that bunch.
That was on the "Memories of Goodman and Miller", wasn't it?
This was '52, on the first series. Don Lamond did most of them and I guess Don couldn't make one session and Ray did.
You could tell now by listening to it, because he had a style.
He had taken over the Miller band after Glenn didn't cross the channel that day.
The Army air force, you mean?
And for the most part, people in that, Peanuts Hucko, but along with that, people who had been with him before the war, but it turned out to be a very good band.
I enjoyed writing for Ray; I always liked Ray.
